svg.text: Connectivity-based boundary read — stationary points come FIRST
1 · Field ψ(R,Z)
harmonic plasma flux + thick-cylinder coil flux (known currents)
2 · Stationary points: ∇ψ = 0
O-points (extrema) + X-points (saddles), split by the Hessian sign.
A LOCAL differential property — found with NO boundary.
3 · Candidate boundary fluxes
{ ψ at each in-vessel X-point } ∪ { limiter-tangency ψ }
one flux value per candidate bounding surface
4 · Connectivity test (trace contour)
confined component = level-set piece containing the axis.
Closes inside the vessel → DIVERTED (X-point bounds it);
touches the limiter first → LIMITED (wall tangency bounds it).
5 · LCFS + topology class
outermost closed surface enclosing the axis that does
NOT cross the limiter → boundary ψ, X-point set,
8-angle radii. Far-field spurious saddles fail the test.
No chicken-and-egg
The proposed order — contour → boundary
→ stationary points — is circular. Reverse it:
• Stationary points need only ∇ψ=0 (step 2),
a local property of the field — independent
of any contour or boundary.
• Contours are traced AFTERWARD (step 4), to
test which stationary point (or the limiter)
actually bounds the axis by connectivity.
• The boundary is thus DEFINED by the stationary
points + connectivity — it is never needed to
FIND them. The dependency runs one way.
